transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start time: 10:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ariel Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dana Ruiz (Acme Head of ML), Ken O'Reilly (Acme Platform), Maya Singh (Acme SecOps), Tom Bauer (Acme Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy): Quick sync on model pinning decisions. Benchmarks updated. Agreed to share docs and schedule canary/rollback playbook.

00:00 Ariel Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the latest benchmarks we ran this week.
00:18 Dana Ruiz: Hi Ariel, hi Samir, thanks. We're mostly interested in the model pinning discussion today - want to avoid surprises during the pilot.
00:27 Samir Patel: Great, I have a slide with the three finalists: Llama-3-70B-q4 (dedicated), Mistral-instruct-xxl-q4, and a smaller hosted variant we've been calling gpt-4o-sim for latency comparisons. Note that q4 quant here refers to per-tensor quantization, results slightly noisy.
00:55 Ken O'Reilly: Quick question — are those measurements on Dedicated infra or Hosted? We saw different p90s last week when you switched VMs.
01:10 Samir Patel: These were run on a Redwood Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) with continuous batching enabled; the hosted variant numbers are from our multi-tenant service with tighter latency SLOs but slightly higher cost per token.
01:33 Ariel Chen: I'll drop the benchmark link in chat after the call: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-poc (note: placeholder link). The CSV has p50/p90/p99, token cost, and quality eval by your prompt set.
01:48 Tom Bauer: We ran the baseline prompts yesterday, but we need more context — like long conversation lengths; how does the KV cache affect cost?
02:05 Samir Patel: The KV cache reduces repeated prefix compute; for long conversations it materially drops token compute after warmup. We show both cold-start and warmed-up metrics in the sheet.
02:33 Maya Singh: From security side, we need to know about encryption in transit and at rest, KMS support, and audit log retention. Any change in model variant that touches our logs is a compliance question.
02:50 Lina Gomez: We'll send the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide post-call; I think Maya asked for the exact retention windows?
03:01 Maya Singh: Yeah and whether audit logs include per-request metadata and masked prompts.
03:15 Ariel Chen: Good callout; audit logs have request id, timestamp, model variant, and latency; we can mask or redact prompt text per your policy — we'll add notes in the doc.
03:34 Dana Ruiz: Back to models — we saw slightly higher hallucination rate on the q4-quant Llama run, is that right?
03:48 Samir Patel: There was a measurable uptick on some narrow-domain prompts; q4 quantization can slightly alter token probabilities. But the smaller hosted variant had better base quality on those prompts at the cost of ~30% higher per-token price.
04:10 Dana Ruiz: So tradeoff is cost vs quality vs latency. Our success criteria is primarily quality for 90% of prompts, with latency p90 under 300ms if possible.
04:27 Ariel Chen: Noted. We can pin the model variant that meets your quality bar and use fallbacks to the hosted variant if quality drops beyond threshold. That gives you a cost-optimized primary with a reliable fallback.
04:46 Ken O'Reilly: How do fallbacks work automatically? If we pin Llama-3-70B-q4 and it degrades, do you auto-swap or just alert us?
05:01 Samir Patel: We support both. For the POC we recommend an automated fallback policy that checks recent quality metrics against baselines (your prompt set). If drift > X% or error rate spikes, it routes to a pinned fallback model or the hosted pool. We can keep the original pinned model in the fleet for rollback testing.
05:28 Tom Bauer: I want a canary rollout plan — e.g., route 1% of traffic to new variant, check latency/cost/quality over 24 hours, then ramp.
05:39 Samir Patel: Agreed; we'll draft a canary playbook. It includes traffic slices, monitoring alerts (p50/p90 latency, quality score, error rate), and automatic rollback conditions.
06:00 Dana Ruiz: What's involved in pinning exactly? Is it just an entry in your catalog or do you need a freeze on the infra side?
06:12 Ariel Chen: Pinning is a config in Redwood Console: it maps your route to a specific model and version. For Dedicated, you can pin to a specific binary/quantization profile; for Hosted, you pin to a specific model alias. Pinning doesn't require infra freeze but you can combine with release windows.
06:32 Maya Singh: In terms of security, if we pin to a Dedicated pool, is the data kept in our VPC? We need separation for regulatory reasons.
06:42 Samir Patel: Yes — Dedicated is customer-isolated and can be deployed inside your VPC or on a private subnet; for on-prem we provide an appliance option. We'll share the architecture note.
07:01 Ken O'Reilly: We noticed a 20% difference in cost between Llama-3-70B-q4 on Dedicated and the hosted small variant. Can you break down token cost vs infra amortization?
07:18 Ariel Chen: The spreadsheet breaks down per-token inference compute cost + sharing overhead + network egress. The Dedicated per-token raw compute is lower, but there's a fixed reserved cost if you commit capacity. For the short pilot, hosted might be cheaper overall unless you run steady high throughput.
07:38 Dana Ruiz: Our expected load is spiky — mostly daytime business hours. We care about P99 latency for peak spikes. How does batching affect P99?
07:52 Samir Patel: Batching optimizes throughput but can increase tail latency in bursty traffic. We can do adaptive batching with a latency budget to control p99. For dedicated pools, we can configure pre-warmed workers to reduce tail.
08:15 Tom Bauer: Can you simulate our traffic pattern? We can provide trace logs.
08:21 Dana Ruiz: Yes we'll share a week of anonymized traces.
08:25 Samir Patel: Perfect — send them to the SE mailbox and we'll run a workload-shaped benchmark.
08:40 Ariel Chen: Quick note — we ran a targeted eval on your prompt set: quality score delta between Llama-3-70B-q4 and hosted-sim was about 4% on accuracy, but cost delta was ~28% lower for q4 on Dedicated once warmed.
09:05 Dana Ruiz: 4% is in the margin for some of our critical prompts; not sure acceptable.
09:12 Samir Patel: We recommend pinning a conservative variant initially — e.g., Llama-3-70B-q4 but with a fallback to hosted-sim for queries flagged by a quality classifier. That reduces exposure.
09:34 Ken O'Reilly: Who runs the quality classifier? On customer side or Redwood?
09:40 Samir Patel: We can supply a simple classifier in the POC that runs post-response and flags likely regressions based on n-gram overlap and hallucination heuristics. You can also plug in your own metrics.
10:05 Maya Singh: For compliance, we need to know retention and redaction options for prompts the classifier stores.
10:12 Lina Gomez: We'll document retention; default is 30 days but enterprise can extend/shorten and we support redaction on ingest.
10:23 Tom Bauer: Let's talk about rollbacks — if we pin and then notice quality drift after a model refresh, what are manual rollback steps?
10:33 Samir Patel: Manual rollback is in Console: select previous version and press rollback. Automated rollback can be configured with policy thresholds — e.g., revert if quality window drops by >5% over last 1,000 requests. We'll include playbook steps and sample CLI commands.
11:00 Dana Ruiz: We also need a way to A/B test two variants during pilot for apples-to-apples quality.
11:08 Samir Patel: Console supports route split with sampling keys; we can do stratified sampling by user or by prompt category. We'll show an example in the canary doc.
11:25 Ariel Chen: Any concerns about vendor lock-in? They sometimes come up with model-specific tooling.
11:32 Ken O'Reilly: Especially with pinning and custom quant profiles, we need to ensure portability.
11:38 Samir Patel: Our approach is to expose abstract model aliases and provide exportable model artifacts where permissible; for dedicated on-prem we can hand over the quantized binaries under the agreement. We'll include portability notes.
11:55 Dana Ruiz: OK, so immediate next steps for us: provide the prompt set, confirm SLOs, and review the benchmark CSV. For Redwood: share benchmark sheet, canary playbook, and security pack.
12:12 Lina Gomez: I'll email the SOC2 summary and KMS guide after the call, and Ariel will send the benchmark link.
12:22 Maya Singh: Please include exact fields in audit logs and an example of redaction.
12:30 Ariel Chen: Noted, we'll add a sample log entry.
12:35 Tom Bauer: One more Q — model catalog naming is sometimes confusing; can we get a short glossary of model names and quant tags?
12:42 Samir Patel: Yes, glossary part of the spreadsheet. We'll annotate the q4/q8 suffixes and model aliases.
12:51 Dana Ruiz: Sounds good. If we agree to pin Llama-3-70B-q4 for the pilot with fallback to hosted-sim, what do you need to set that up?
13:02 Samir Patel: We'll need your route name, desired pin timestamp/window, and whether to enable automatic fallback or manual alert. Also acceptance criteria thresholds.
13:18 Ken O'Reilly: We'll start with manual fallback but prefer automated after the first week.
13:24 Ariel Chen: Great. Lina — can you send a meeting invite next week to review canary playbook?
13:30 Lina Gomez: Yep, I'll schedule follow-up for 09/15.
13:35 Ariel Chen: Recap: Redwood to share benchmark CSV + glossary + canary doc + security pack. Acme to share prompt set + traffic trace + confirm SLOs. Action owners captured in the meeting notes. Any final Qs?
13:55 Dana Ruiz: No, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the spreadsheet.
14:02 Tom Bauer: Thanks.
14:10 Meeting ends.
